statement.p: Compute the Jacobian of : \Phi(r,\theta) = (3 r\cos\theta,7 r\sin\theta)

static.solution: x=3 r \cos \theta and y=7 r \sin \theta, the Jacobian of \Phi is the following determinant: \mathrm{Jac}(\Phi) = \frac{\partial ( x,y )}{\partial ( r,\theta )}= \left|\begin{array}{rr} \frac{\partial x}{\partial r}\amp \frac{\partial x}{\partial \theta }\\ \noalign{\medskip} \frac{\partial y}{\partial r}\amp \frac{\partial y}{\partial \theta }\end{array}\right|= \left|\begin{array}{cc} 3\cos \theta \amp -3 r \sin \theta \\ 7\sin \theta \amp 7 r \cos \theta \end{array}\right|=3\cdot 7\cdot r \cos^2\theta +3\cdot 7\cdot r \sin^2\theta = 3\cdot 7\cdot r(\cos^2\theta +\sin^2\theta )= 21\cdot r\cdot 1=21 r
